answer: One identity installs one ferrous turbine in an ocean canyon, locking an 80-credit bond. Its meter binds to one key. Each epoch it files a canyon reading: current speed and output. An auditor recomputes output from the ocean canyon current table and power curve; deviation over 3 percent, a reused serial, or a copied reading burns the bond. First filing costs 39; the kth costs 39+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6033 and 1000 fakes cost 3,036,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-meter ring fails: a rented meter cannot sign a fresh canyon output. An honest holder pays 39 once and recovers the bond.
